methodology: The original research topic and the generated technical specification were decomposed into atomic units by identifying individual requirements, features, behaviors, and constraints. Each atomic unit is designed to be independent, self-contained, technically specific, unambiguous, and implementable as a single requirement. This involved dissecting the text into discrete statements about the system's functionality, inputs, outputs, and operational rules. For the original research topic, the decomposition focused on extracting the core requirements and constraints from the problem description and the provided Verilog code. For the generated technical specification, the decomposition focused on extracting information from the header analysis, combinational logic function, enhanced combinational description, and timing logic summary.
mindtraced_atomic_units: The system consists of a one-dimensional array of 512 cells (q[511:0])
Each cell can be either on (1) or off (0)
The state of the entire system advances by one time step on each clock cycle
The next state of each cell is determined by its current state and the states of its two immediate neighbors, according to the Rule 110 transition table
Boundary cells beyond the 512-cell array are assumed to be off (0)
A synchronous active-high load input allows the initial state of the system to be loaded from the data[511:0] input
spec_atomic_units: Module implements a 512-cell Rule 110 cellular automaton
Module has synchronous active-high load input load
Output q is updated synchronously on the rising edge of clk
When load is high, register q is loaded with the value of data on the rising edge of clk
When load is low, register q is updated with the next state of the cellular automaton based on the current state of q and the Rule 110 logic, also on the rising edge of clk
Combinational logic implements the Rule 110 update rule for each cell
For each cell q[i], its next state depends on the current states of q[i-1], q[i], and q[i+1]
Boundary conditions are such that q[-1] and q[512] are always zero
For cell q[0], the left neighbor q[-1] is assumed to be 0
For cell q[511], the right neighbor q[512] is assumed to be 0
